Overview

GitHub's Core UX organization owns the frontend platform behind GitHub.com: the architecture, tooling, and standards that let hundreds of engineers ship UI that is fast, accessible, consistent, and reliable. You'll partner closely with other Principal and Staff engineers, Engineering Managers, and Product and Design leadership to decide where the platform goes next and to drive that direction to real, shipped outcomes.

Overview

AI writes code faster than teams can review it, and review is now the bottleneck. Getting an agent to review as well as, or better than, a great engineer who knows your codebase is one of the most important unsolved problems in AI-assisted development.

Copilot code review is GitHub's answer, and more developers get reviews from it than from any other AI reviewer, increasingly on code that agents wrote. Getting review right is hard to define and harder to measure, and no single number settles whether reviews got better. We think the AI products that win are the ones with the best evals, and we're building the best, offline and online.

We run at GitHub scale with an on-call rotation, and we're a fast-growing team competing to build the best AI code reviewer in the world.

Responsibilities

  • Improve how the agent reviews: the context it uses, what it remembers, and how it handles a pull request as it changes over time.

  • Prove changes with offline and online evals and help sharpen the evals themselves.
  • Work on the end-to-end review experience developers use in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot CLI, and on pull requests.

  • Experience partnering with product and feature teams to improve the reliability and scalability of what they ship.
  • Ability to influence engineering decisions and proactively engage in system design conversations.
  • Experience running stateful services on managed cloud data stores, specifically Azure Cosmos DB and Azure SQL Database, or equivalents such as DynamoDB, Aurora, or Cloud Spanner, with a focus on partition and index design, consistency tradeoffs, and throughput provisioning.
  • Experience diagnosing and resolving application-level scalability problems: N+1 query patterns, hot partitions, unbounded fan-out, cache stampedes, and data access patterns that don't scale.
  • Experience building internal tooling, SDKs, or libraries used by other engineering teams, written in production-grade Go, Python, Ruby, or Rust.
  • Familiarity with the failure modes of large-scale systems, both in the application and in the platform beneath it e.g. cascading failures, retry storms, thundering herds, partial outages, throttling and quota limits, control plane outages, noisy neighbors, and the patterns that mitigate them.
  • Experience contributing to cloud migrations of live services, including dual-write and backfill strategies, traffic shifting, and rollback planning.
  • Effective communication skills and willingness to pair on problems, brainstorm in public, and enthusiastically engage with your teammates in group problem solving.
